title: Exact Compatibility Geometry of Three-Qubit Entanglement
authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong, Ming Yang
abstract: We present a permutation-symmetric supporting relation between the pairwise concurrences and the three-tangle in three-qubit system, whose extrema are attained only by the symmetric $W$ and GHZ local-unitary classes. Furthermore, by introducing the concept of a four-dimensional compatibility body, we show that our proposed global relation and the previous CKW relation can be uniformly viewed as different supporting directions of the same achievable set. Subsequently, we provide a necessary-and-sufficient semi-algebraic characterization of the complete four-dimensional compatibility of a three-qubit pure state. Based on this, we can conversely describe the compatibility between entangled components: given the remaining entangled components, the missing two-body entangled component can only take values within a precise parameter-free interval. We demonstrate that the above construction also applies to arbitrary concurrence-generated entanglement measures.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes the geometric constraints governing the entanglement structure of three-qubit pure states. It moves beyond simple upper bounds by deriving necessary and sufficient semi-algebraic conditions for the coexistence of pairwise concurrences and the three-tangle. The results provide exact formulas to determine the possible range of a missing entanglement component given the others.
main_problem: To determine the fundamental, necessary, and sufficient constraints governing the coexistence of multiple entanglement measures (pairwise concurrences and three-tangle) in a three-qubit pure state.
main_result: The paper provides a necessary-and-sufficient semi-algebraic characterization for the entire achievable entanglement region ($\Omega_3$) and derives exact, parameter-free intervals for missing bipartite entanglement components.
method: The authors use supporting geometry, canonical state parametrization (Ac´ın form), and algebraic elimination techniques to characterize the boundary of the entanglement region.
model_or_system: The study focuses on three-qubit pure quantum states, $|\psiangle_{ABC}$, and the entanglement measures associated with them, such as pairwise concurrences ($C_{ij}$) and the three-tangle ($	au_3$).
key_observables: Pairwise concurrences ($C_{AB}, C_{AC}, C_{BC}$) and the three-tangle ($	au_3$).
important_parameters: The state is analyzed in a four-dimensional compatibility body ($\Omega_3$), and the analysis involves auxiliary parameters ($s$) and transformed variables ($X, Y, Z$).
main_assumptions: The final characterization relies on the Ac´ın standard form parametrization and the existence of an auxiliary parameter $s$ to define the boundary conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate cross-sections of the three-qubit entanglement region in the space of squared concurrences for varying $	au_3$, showing how GHZ correlations constrain pairwise entanglement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing initial global supporting linear constraints (Theorem 1) to deriving the full, non-linear, necessary-and-sufficient semi-algebraic characterization (Theorem 2), culminating in the exact determination of completion intervals for missing entanglement components.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to map out the precise boundaries of entanglement resource spaces, which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum correlations in multi-partite systems.
